title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: v1.16.0 adds hover documentation for @Suppress annotations, dispatcher-specific badges on coroutine suspend call markers, and default keyboard shortcuts for common navigation and editor actions.

highlights.title: @Suppress Hover Docs
highlights.description: Hovering over any suppression ID inside @Suppress, @SuppressLint, or @SuppressWarnings now shows a plain-English explanation of the warning being silenced — no need to look it up externally.
highlights.mediaAlt: Hover tooltip showing a plain-English explanation of a suppression ID

highlights.title: Dispatcher Badges
highlights.description: Suspend call markers now display a dispatcher-specific badge on coroutine builder invocations that name a dispatcher, making it immediately clear which dispatcher each suspension point is tied to.
highlights.mediaAlt: Suspend call markers with dispatcher badges inline

highlights.title: Default Keybindings
highlights.description: Common Kotlin Jump actions now have default keyboard shortcuts — Find Usages, Go to Test, Navigate Back/Forward, Organize Imports, and more — reducing reliance on the command palette.

sections.heading: Features
bullets: Added hover documentation for @Suppress, @SuppressLint, and @SuppressWarnings annotation IDs — hovering over a suppression string shows a plain-English description of the Kotlin compiler warning, Android Lint check, or Java warning being silenced.
Added dispatcher-specific inlay badges to coroutine builder calls that name a dispatcher, so dispatched suspension points are visually distinct from plain suspend calls at a glance.

Registered default keyboard shortcuts for common actions: Find Usages (Alt+F7), Go to Test (Alt+Shift+T), Go to Composable Preview (Alt+Shift+P), Organize Imports (Shift+Alt+O), Rename (Ctrl/Cmd+R), Navigate Back/Forward (Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+←/→), Copy FQN (Shift+Alt+C), and Toggle Inline Features (Shift+Alt+I).
